FISH_TELLS.fresh: Fresh. The flesh is clear and bright with its feeling.
FISH_TELLS.past: Dull and milky. Past its best.

knead.label: KNEAD
knead.line: Fold and push in time. Stop when a stretched piece lets the light through without tearing.
tells: Shaggy. The dough tears and sticks to the board.
Smooth. The dough springs back slowly when pressed.
Windowpane. A stretched piece lets light through without tearing.
Too tight. The dough tears instead of stretching. Let it rest.
knead.tradeoff: Underworked bread is dense; overworked is tough.

proof.label: PROOF
proof.line: Leave it somewhere warm. Press a floured finger in: ready when the dent springs back slowly.
tells: The dent springs straight back. Not ready.
The dent fills back slowly. Ready.
The dent stays. Over-proofed.
Collapsed. It rose too long and sank.
proof.tradeoff: A longer proof is more flavour and risks collapse.

bake.label: BAKE
bake.line: Steam it early for the rise, then take it out when the crust is deep brown and it knocks hollow.
tells: Pale and soft.
Golden. It knocks dull.
Deep brown, and it knocks hollow.
Dark at the edges. It smells of scorch.
Black.
bake.tradeoff: A darker crust is more flavour, nearer burnt.

roll.label: ROLL
roll.line: Roll it thinner pass by pass. Hold it to the light: stop when you can see your hand through it.
tells: Thick as a biscuit. No light comes through.
Even, but the light stops at it.
Thin enough. Print shows through the sheet.
Paper thin. The edges are starting to tear.
roll.tradeoff: Thinner is silkier and cooks faster, nearer torn.

laminate.label: LAMINATE
laminate.line: Fold the sheet and roll it again; each fold doubles its layers. Stop when it is smooth as satin, square at the edges.
tells: Ragged edges, a rough face.
The edges straighten.
Smooth as satin, square at the edges.
Tight and rubbery. It springs back from the roller.
laminate.tradeoff: More folds is more bite, until it fights you.

cut.label: CUT
cut.line: Cut ribbons a finger wide, every one the same.
tells: Thread-thin, like angel hair.
Narrow: tagliolini.
Even ribbons, a finger wide.
Broad: pappardelle.
Ragged and uneven.
cut.tradeoff: The cut sets how the sauce clings.

pull.label: PULL
pull.line: Stretch the rope, fold it in two and stretch again: each pull doubles the strands. Stop before it snaps.
tells: One thick rope.
Four strands, thick as a finger.
Sixteen strands, round as chopsticks.
Sixty-four strands, thin as string.
Two hundred and fifty-six, thread-fine. It is near snapping.

moments.snap: A strand snapped. The dough needs more rest.

pull.tradeoff: Finer noodles need more gluten: knead well first or they snap.

boil.label: BOIL
boil.line: Boil in water salted like the sea. Bite one: take it out while a thin white thread is left at its heart.
tells: Raw. It snaps.
It bends, chalky all through.
Al dente. A thin white core at the bite.
Soft all the way through. Overcooked.
Mush.
boil.tradeoff: Al dente keeps its bite and its soul; a minute more and both are gone.

sear.label: SEAR
sear.line: Skin down in a hot pan. Do not move it: it lets go of the pan by itself when the crust is made.
tells: Grey, stuck to the pan.
The skin tightens. It still clings.
Golden, and it lets go of the pan by itself.
Dark. The edge smokes.
Black.
sear.tradeoff: A deeper crust is more flavour, nearer burnt.

bleed.label: BLEED
bleed.line: The fish thrashes and stills in turns. Press the spike behind its eye in the still moment: a quick, calm end.
bleed.unit: the moment between thrashes, 0.5 its stillness
tells: It thrashes.
It slows.
Still. Strike now.
It gathers itself again.
bleed.tradeoff: A calm end keeps the flesh sweet: rigor comes later and less lactic acid sours it.

simmer.label: SIMMER
simmer.line: Do nothing, correctly: keep the dial low so the pot barely trembles. A bubble that rolls is a boil, and a boil ruins it.
tells: Barely warm. Nothing moves.
The first wisp of steam.
A few bubbles at the pot's edge: a trembling simmer.
Bubbles rising steadily. Too far for kombu.
A rolling boil.
simmer.tradeoff: A longer, lower simmer is deeper; a hotter one is quicker and nearer bitter.

rice.label: RICE
rice.line: Rinse the rice and pour the water off until it runs almost clear. Then set the water to the line on the pot.
tells: The water is milk-white.
Cloudy. It still clouds the pot.
Almost clear, a faint haze.
Clear as water.
rice.tradeoff: None: rice is the honest move.

steep.label: STEEP
steep.line: Watch the water, not a clock. Pour when the bubbles are the right size for the leaf.
tells: Still water, a few tiny beads on the pot: "shrimp eyes".
Bubbles the size of crab eyes. The first wisp of steam.
Fish eyes, with a hush: the water is hot, not boiling.
A rope of pearls rising from the bottom.
Rolling boil. It will scald the leaf.
steep.tradeoff: Hotter water is stronger and more bitter.

sugar.label: SUGAR
sugar.line: Boil the syrup and drop a spoon of it in cold water to read it. Take it off at the stage you want.
sugar.unit: syrup stage (soft ball 112-116 C .. hard crack 146-154 C)
tells: The spoon dissolves. Still only sugar water.
A thread, no more.
A soft ball: it holds, and flattens in the fingers.
A hard ball, firm and chewy.
Hard crack: it snaps like glass.
Amber going dark. It smells of caramel, then smoke.
sugar.tradeoff: A harder stage keeps longer and is less tender.

roux.label: ROUX
roux.line: Equal flour and fat, stirred. Keep it moving or it scorches. Stop at the colour you want.
tells: White, smelling of raw flour.
Blond, a biscuit smell.
Peanut-butter brown. Nutty.
Dark chocolate. A quarter of white's thickening.
Scorched. It smells burnt.
roux.tradeoff: Darker is more flavour and less body.

emulsion.label: EMULSION
emulsion.line: Pour the oil in a thin thread while you whisk. Pour only as fast as the whisk can take it.
emulsion.unit: oil taken, held by the whisk
tells: Yolk and a few drops of oil.
Pale and loose. It is taking the oil.
Glossy and thick, ribbons off the whisk.
Stiff, nearly too much oil.
emulsion.tradeoff: The one rhythm move: a rescue costs a yolk.

ferment.label: FERMENT
ferment.line: Koji works on its own clock, warm. Set the warmth now and then; take it out before it spores.
tells: Rice and white threads, a sweet smell of chestnut.
A white bloom, warm to the hand. It smells of apples.
Fully white, sweet and mushroomy. Ready.
Yellow-green flecks. It is starting to spore.
Spored. Bitter and spent.
ferment.tradeoff: Longer is deeper and sweeter, with less bite.

smoke.label: SMOKE
smoke.line: Keep the fire low and fed. Thin blue smoke is good; white, heavy smoke is bad.
smoke.unit: fire low and fed, thin blue smoke
tells: Nearly out. Only a thread of grey.
Thin blue smoke curling up. Good.
Thicker. It is turning white.
Heavy white smoke. It will taste bitter.
